words.definition: A skilled maker who builds, repairs, or invents clever objects by hand.
words.example: The ship's artificer could rebuild a shattered engine valve from a few scraps in the hold.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'art officer' — an officer of the crafting arts who fashions clever devices.

words.definition: A person who is deeply devoted to beauty and fine art.
words.example: A committed aesthete, he rearranged the whole room so each vase caught the afternoon light.
words.mnemonic: Say it 'ess-theet' — an 'athlete' of beauty, always in training to admire the finer things.

words.definition: Relating to beauty or the enjoyment of things that look pleasing.
words.example: The architect kept the glass staircase for purely aesthetic reasons, though it served no real purpose.
words.mnemonic: From Greek 'aisthesis' (perception) — think of what pleases the senses when you perceive it.

words.definition: Outstanding technical skill, especially in performing music or art.
words.example: Her violin solo showed such virtuosity that the orchestra paused just to watch her fingers fly.
words.mnemonic: 'VIRTUE + osity' — the shining virtue of jaw-dropping technical mastery.

words.definition: A performer or artist with exceptional, dazzling technical ability.
words.example: Only a virtuoso could tear through that concerto at full tempo without a single wrong note.
words.mnemonic: 'Virtue' + 'so' good — an Italian maestro whose skill is simply virtue perfected.

words.definition: An artwork that openly imitates or blends the styles of other works.
words.example: His debut film is a loving pastiche of 1940s noir, stitching together tropes from a dozen classics.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'paste-iche' — bits and pieces pasted together from other people's work.

words.definition: The bold contrast of light and shade used in drawing or painting.
words.example: Caravaggio mastered chiaroscuro, letting a single shaft of light strike a face plunged in darkness.
words.mnemonic: Italian 'chiaro' (light/clear) + 'oscuro' (dark) — literally light-dark.

words.definition: The imitation or representation of real life in art and literature.
words.example: Greek tragedy depended on mimesis, holding a mirror up to human suffering onstage.
words.mnemonic: Root of 'mimic' and 'mime' — MIME-sis is the art of copying life.

words.definition: A thin surface film or sheen that forms on metal or wood over time.
words.example: The old bronze horseman had taken on a soft green patina after a century in the rain.
words.mnemonic: 'PAT-ina' — years of gentle 'pats' from weather leave a mellow coating on the surface.

words.definition: Delicate decorative work made from fine twisted threads of gold or silver.
words.example: The locket's silver filigree was so fine it looked like frozen lace on her palm.
words.mnemonic: 'Fili-' means thread (like 'filament') — threads twisted into lacy grain.

words.definition: An ornate design of intertwined flowing lines, leaves, and scrollwork.
words.example: The mosque's walls swirled with arabesques that drew the eye endlessly upward and inward.
words.mnemonic: 'Arab-esque' — in the style of Arabic and Islamic ornament, all winding vines and curves.

words.definition: Extremely ornate and elaborate, full of curved, fanciful decoration.
words.example: The palace's rococo ceilings dripped with gilded cherubs, shells, and curling vines.
words.mnemonic: From French 'rocaille' (rock-and-shell work) — say 'ro-CO-co' and picture frilly, over-the-top shell curves.

words.definition: Highly elaborate, dramatic, and extravagant in style or detail.
words.example: The cathedral's baroque altar overwhelmed visitors with twisting columns and gilded flourishes.
words.mnemonic: From Portuguese 'barroco', an irregular pearl — 'ba-ROKE' means richly imperfect and overdone.

words.definition: An object or detail added to something to make it look more attractive.
words.example: She hung a glass ornament on the tree that scattered little rainbows across the room.
words.mnemonic: 'ORN-' shares roots with 'adorn' — an add-on that adorns and dresses something up.

words.definition: Serving as decoration rather than having a practical use.
words.example: The garden's ornamental hedges were clipped into peacocks purely to delight the eye.
words.mnemonic: 'Adorn + mental' — picture a mantel of trinkets kept only to be admired, never used.

words.definition: To make something more attractive by adding extra details, or to exaggerate a story.
words.example: She couldn't resist embellishing the plain white cake with sugar roses and gold leaf.
words.mnemonic: Em-BELL-ish — imagine hanging little BELLs all over a plain dress to pretty it up.

words.definition: To add beauty or decoration to a person, place, or object.
words.example: Gold bracelets and jasmine flowers adorned the bride's wrists and hair.
words.mnemonic: A-DORN sounds like 'a door' — picture decorating a DOOR with a festive wreath.

words.definition: To hang chains of flowers, ribbons, or streamers across a space as decoration.
words.example: They festooned the entire hall with paper lanterns and looping streamers for the reunion.
words.mnemonic: FESTOON = 'FESTive + balloon' — think garlands and balloons strung up for a festival.

words.definition: To dress or decorate in a flashy, gaudy, and often tasteless way.
words.example: The carnival float was bedizened with clashing neon ribbons, sequins, and blinking lights.
words.mnemonic: be-DIZEN → 'be-DAZZLE' someone until they're almost dizzy from too much glitter.

words.definition: To cover something with decorations, often lavishly or festively.
words.example: The parade float was bedecked with thousands of fresh roses from front to back.
words.mnemonic: be-DECK — you DECK the halls, covering the whole deck with flags and lights.

words.definition: To polish a surface by rubbing it until it becomes smooth and shiny.
words.example: He burnished the old brass doorknob until he could see his face in it.
words.mnemonic: BURN-ish — rub the metal so hard and fast it nearly BURNs, leaving it gleaming.

words.definition: To coat an object with a hard, glossy, protective finish.
words.example: The artisan lacquered the wooden box in deep red until it gleamed like glass.
words.mnemonic: LACQUER ≈ 'lock her' — the glossy coat locks in and seals the wood beneath.

words.definition: To apply a clear, resin-based coating that gives a glossy protective surface.
words.example: After sanding the table, she varnished it so the wood grain shone through.
words.mnemonic: VARNISH = 'VARN + finish' — the final glossy finish that makes wood glow.

words.definition: To show or describe someone or something in a picture, story, or film.
words.example: The wall mural depicts farmers harvesting wheat beneath a golden evening sky.
words.mnemonic: de-PICT — hidden inside is 'PICTure'; to depict is to put it in a picture.

words.definition: To describe or represent someone in words or art, or to play a character.
words.example: The actor portrayed the aging king with quiet, trembling dignity.
words.mnemonic: por-TRAY — imagine carrying someone's PORTRAIT out on a TRAY to show the room.

words.definition: To produce or represent something, especially in art, or to cause it to become a state.
words.example: The architect rendered the new library in soft watercolor before construction began.
words.mnemonic: REND-er — an artist 'sends' (renders) the finished image out to the screen.

words.definition: To cut or carve a design into a hard surface using acid or a sharp tool.
words.example: The jeweler etched tiny initials into the inside of the silver wedding ring.
words.mnemonic: ETCH sounds like 'itch' — scratching an itch, you scratch fine lines into glass.

words.definition: To decorate a surface with a design that stands out in raised relief.
words.example: The company logo was embossed on the leather cover, raised under your fingertips.
words.mnemonic: em-BOSS — the BOSS's initials stick out, raised proudly, on his fancy notebook.

words.definition: To bring a feeling, memory, or image into someone's mind.
words.example: The smell of pine needles evoked childhood winters at her grandmother's cabin.
words.mnemonic: e-VOKE — from Latin 'vocare', to call; it calls a memory out of you like a voice.

words.definition: A recurring theme, image, or decorative pattern in art, music, or writing.
words.example: A floral motif repeated across the wallpaper, the curtains, and the dinner plates.
words.mnemonic: MOTIF sounds like 'motive' — a recurring idea that keeps driving the whole design.

words.definition: A striking scene or group of people arranged as if in a still picture.
words.example: As the curtain rose, the actors froze in a dramatic tableau of the battle's aftermath.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'table' + 'oh' — picture people posed motionless on a table while onlookers gasp 'oh!'

words.definition: A picture or pattern made from many small colored pieces fitted together.
words.example: The cathedral floor was a dazzling mosaic of blue and gold tiles arranged into a phoenix.
words.mnemonic: 'Moses saw' a picture built from tiny stones — MOSAIC = countless little bits forming one image.

words.definition: A brief, evocative description or a short scene capturing a single moment.
words.example: Her memoir offered warm vignettes of childhood summers rather than one continuous narrative.
words.mnemonic: 'Vignette' hides 'vine' — imagine a tiny decorative vine sketch bordering one small page.

words.definition: A drawing or description that exaggerates features for comic or satirical effect.
words.example: The cartoonist gave the senator an enormous nose and a tiny body — a merciless caricature.
words.mnemonic: 'Care-i-cature': the artist doesn't 'care' to be accurate, so features get wildly distorted.

words.definition: A humorous imitation of a work or style, mocking it through exaggeration.
words.example: The sketch was a parody of the evening news, with a bumbling anchor reading fake headlines.
words.mnemonic: Say 'pair-o-dee' — a pair of DJs spoofing a serious hit song for laughs.

words.definition: A theatrical entertainment that mocks serious subjects through exaggeration and comedy.
words.example: The troupe's burlesque of grand opera had the whole audience roaring with laughter.
words.mnemonic: 'Burly' + 'esque' — picture a burly man in a tiny tutu, absurdly poking fun at ballet.

words.definition: A grotesque or absurd distortion that debases something meant to be serious.
words.example: Critics called the rushed, evidence-free trial a travesty of justice.
words.mnemonic: From Latin 'trans-vestire,' to dress up in disguise — something serious dressed up as a farce.

words.definition: An exact copy or reproduction of something, especially written or printed material.
words.example: The museum displayed a facsimile of the Declaration so the fragile original could stay locked away.
words.mnemonic: Latin 'fac simile' = 'make similar' — the same root that gave us 'fax,' which sends copies.

words.definition: A close reproduction or model of an original object.
words.example: He built a scale replica of the Eiffel Tower entirely from matchsticks.
words.mnemonic: Share the root of 'replicate' — to make again, producing a stand-in of the real thing.

words.definition: A crude model or sculpture representing a hated or specific person.
words.example: Protesters burned an effigy of the dictator in the town square.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'a figure' — a stuffed fake figure of someone, often set alight in protest.

words.definition: Full of sly cunning and deceit; skilled at tricking others.
words.example: The guileful merchant hid the coin's flaws until the sale was final.
words.mnemonic: A 'guy full' of tricks — a guy full of guile who cannot be trusted.

words.definition: Superficially attractive but cheap, gaudy, and lacking real value.
words.example: The mansion's gilded fixtures struck her as meretricious — all glitter and no taste.
words.mnemonic: From Latin 'meretrix' (a prostitute) — flashy, tawdry allure meant only to lure.

words.definition: Serving as an artificial and usually inferior substitute for the real thing.
words.example: During the war, families drank ersatz coffee brewed from roasted acorns.
words.mnemonic: German for 'replacement' — say 'her-sats,' a poor stand-in slipped in for the real deal.

words.definition: Deliberately created or contrived rather than arising naturally or genuinely.
words.example: The stock's factitious surge was engineered by traders spreading false rumors.
words.mnemonic: 'Fact' + Latin 'facere' (to make) — literally 'made up,' manufactured to look real.

words.definition: An image or representation of something, often a poor or superficial imitation of the real thing.
words.example: The theme park's Eiffel Tower was a simulacrum, cheap and half the height of the Paris original.
words.mnemonic: "simulate" + "crumb" — a mere simulated crumb standing in for the genuine article.

words.definition: An absurd pretense meant to deceive others but easily seen through.
words.example: Their warm public handshake was a charade; behind closed doors each was plotting the other's downfall.
words.mnemonic: The party game 'charades' — everyone acts out something fake while others watch.

words.definition: Artificial behavior or manner put on to impress or mislead people.
words.example: His sudden British accent was pure affectation, since he had never left Ohio in his life.
words.mnemonic: Say it as "a-FAKE-tation" — a fake presentation of yourself.

words.definition: Behaving in an artificial way to impress; not genuine or natural.
words.example: She greeted her guests with an affected drawl that convinced absolutely no one.
words.mnemonic: Hear it as "a-FAKE-ted" — the manner has been faked.

words.definition: To plan or create something cleverly, often through scheming or with difficulty.
words.example: She managed to contrive an excuse and slipped out of the party unseen.
words.mnemonic: "con" + "drive" — you drive a con, engineering a scheme step by step.

words.definition: A clever trick or plan used to outwit an enemy or gain advantage.
words.example: The general's stratagem lured the enemy cavalry into a narrow, muddy valley.
words.mnemonic: "strategy" + "gem" — a gem of a battle strategy (Greek 'stratos' = army).

words.definition: Clever and skillful, especially in a cunning or deceptive way.
words.example: With one artful remark, he shifted all the blame onto his rival.
words.mnemonic: "art" + "full" — full of the fine art of cunning.

words.definition: Skilled at using tricks to get what one wants; slyly clever.
words.example: The crafty salesman talked them into buying gadgets they would never use.
words.mnemonic: Think of a witch's dark "craft" — cunning tricks brewed up.

words.definition: Cleverly deceitful; showing a secretive, cunning nature.
words.example: With a sly grin, she slipped the last cookie behind her back.
words.mnemonic: A "sly" fox that slides silently and secretly toward the henhouse.

words.definition: Skillful use of the hands in performing tricks; clever deception.
words.example: With dazzling legerdemain, the magician made the borrowed watch vanish into thin air.
words.mnemonic: French "léger de main" = light of hand — light-fingered trickery.

words.definition: Skillful, quick finger movements used to perform magic tricks.
words.example: The street performer's prestidigitation had the crowd hunting for hidden wires and mirrors.
words.mnemonic: "presto" + "digit" — Presto! done with your nimble digits (fingers).

words.definition: Dexterity or cunning, especially in deceiving or performing tricks.
words.example: By sleight of hand, the dealer slid an extra card from the bottom of the deck.
words.mnemonic: Looks like "slight" — a slight, lightning-quick motion of the hands.

words.definition: To deceive or trick someone in order to gain something.
words.example: The con artist tried to cozen the widow out of her life savings.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like "cousin" — that shady cousin who always cheats you at cards.

words.definition: A calculated opening move or remark made to gain an advantage.
words.example: Offering free samples was the café's gambit to hook passing commuters.
words.mnemonic: The chess "gambit" — sacrifice a pawn early to seize the upper hand.

words.definition: An unrealistic hope or fanciful mental creation that cannot actually exist.
words.example: Finding a tax system everyone calls fair may be a chimera, but reformers keep chasing it.
words.mnemonic: A fire-breathing Greek beast stitched from lion, goat, and snake — an impossible mashup that could never really exist.

words.definition: Existing only in the imagination; wildly fanciful and impossible to achieve.
words.example: His chimerical scheme to tow an iceberg to the desert drew polite nods and no funding.
words.mnemonic: Like a chimera, that mythical impossible beast — so the adjective describes dreams that can't be real.

words.definition: Based on a false impression; seeming real but not actually so.
words.example: The thirsty traveler's oasis turned out to be illusory, dissolving as he stumbled closer.
words.mnemonic: Hides 'illus-' from illusion — a trick of perception that fools the eye.

words.definition: A ghostly figure or image that appears in the mind without being truly present.
words.example: In the fever's grip, a pale phantasm seemed to drift across the foot of her bed.
words.mnemonic: Phantom + -asm — picture the Phantom of the Opera looming as an apparition.

words.definition: Showing complete mastery or perfection in a particular skill or area.
words.example: A consummate diplomat, she defused the shouting match before anyone could raise a fist.
words.mnemonic: Con + summit — someone who has reached the very summit of their craft.

words.definition: Skillful, subtle handling of a situation that demands tact and delicacy.
words.example: She managed the feuding partners with such finesse that both left convinced they'd won.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'fine-ness' — doing the tricky thing with fine, delicate precision.

words.definition: Using lofty, grand language intended to sound impressive.
words.example: The senator's magniloquent address soared with sweeping phrases yet promised nothing concrete.
words.mnemonic: Magni (great) + loqui (to speak) — literally 'great-speaking,' all puffed-up grandeur.

words.definition: Inflated, pompous speech or writing that carries little real substance.
words.example: Beneath the manager's bombast about 'synergy' and 'paradigms' lay no actual plan.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'bomb blast' — a loud explosion of empty, oversized words.

words.definition: Of a voice, full, round, and resonant; of style, pompously inflated.
words.example: The announcer's orotund voice filled the whole stadium without needing a microphone.
words.mnemonic: From Latin 'ore rotundo,' round mouth — think 'rotund,' a big round booming tone.

words.definition: Excessively complicated and intricate, often with hidden or devious workings.
words.example: The agency's byzantine approval process required seven signatures just to order a pencil.
words.mnemonic: Recall the Byzantine Empire's maze of court intrigue — tangled, secretive, endlessly complex.

words.definition: Marked by an artificial, self-conscious style rather than natural behavior.
words.example: His mannered speech, full of studied pauses and flourishes, felt rehearsed and insincere.
words.mnemonic: Full of 'manners' put on for show — style performed rather than genuine.

words.definition: A surface reused for writing on which traces of earlier layers still show through.
words.example: The old city is a palimpsest, Roman walls peeking through medieval brick and modern glass.
words.mnemonic: Greek 'palin' (again) + 'psestos' (scraped) — something scraped clean and written on again.

words.definition: An earlier image or form in a painting that becomes visible beneath later layers.
words.example: A faint pentimento revealed the painter had first set the hand in a different pose.
words.mnemonic: Italian 'pentirsi,' to repent — the canvas 'repents' its first attempt, letting it bleed through.

words.definition: To give off flashing sparkles of light; to shine with brilliant flashes.
words.example: Cut diamonds coruscated under the gallery lamps, throwing tiny rainbows across the walls.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'core-us-skate' — imagine sparks skating and flashing off a polished surface.

words.definition: Shining brilliantly; dazzling and magnificent in appearance.
words.example: The queen entered resplendent in gold silk and a crown studded with emeralds.
words.mnemonic: Re + 'splendid' — something extra splendid, fairly glowing with splendor.

words.definition: Belonging to a small, elite circle far above ordinary experience; also, thin like mountain air.
words.example: The gala drew a rarefied crowd of billionaires, ambassadors, and Nobel laureates.
words.mnemonic: Latin rarus (thin) + facere (make): air 'made thin' high on a peak, where only a select few can breathe — an exclusive height.

words.definition: To smear a surface clumsily with paint, plaster, or another soft substance.
words.example: The toddler daubed thick red paint across the wall in messy streaks.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like an exaggerated 'dab' — but instead of one neat dab, a sloppy glob slapped on.

words.definition: Showy but useless ornamentation, or trivial and frivolous decoration lacking real worth.
words.example: She stripped the dress of its ribbons and bows, impatient with such frippery.
words.mnemonic: Hear 'frilly' inside it — frilly, frivolous finery that adds fuss but no substance.

words.definition: A pretentious, flashy display meant to impress others and attract admiration.
words.example: His gold watches and marble foyer reeked of ostentation rather than taste.
words.mnemonic: Read it as 'OH-STARE-AT-shun' — a showy demand that everyone stop and stare.

words.definition: To put together or concoct something from assorted ingredients, parts, or ideas.
words.example: The chef confected an elaborate dessert from cream, berries, and spun sugar.
words.mnemonic: Think 'confection': a confectioner con- (together) + facere (makes) sweets by combining ingredients.

words.definition: To exaggerate a tale by adding invented or fanciful extra details.
words.example: Each time he retold the fishing trip, he embroidered it with wilder details.
words.mnemonic: You stitch decorative thread onto plain cloth — likewise you stitch fake flourishes onto a plain story.

words.definition: A dazzling display of great skill, boldness, or brilliant technique in performance.
words.example: The pianist ended the concerto with such bravura that the audience leapt to their feet.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'BRAVO!' shouted for a virtuoso — bravura is what earns the bravo.
